A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same critical-confabulation study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original contamination-audit experiments, timeline validation, narrative-cloze evaluations in Table 2, and supplementary analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds stochastic-decoding experiments in Table 3 and shared-error statistics in Section 7.

M1.justification: The contamination audits, GPT-o3 timeline extraction, narrative-cloze procedure, prompt templates, and story-emb scoring remain unchanged. Stochastic decoding is introduced as an evaluation ablation rather than a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BWTC corpus, English historical-document coverage, and 156 character timelines. The new analyses reuse this coverage; partial and n-gram cloze tasks illustrated in v2 already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 18 models, and the paired comparisons in v1 Table 3/v2 Table 4 retain their comparator membership. The stochastic table uses existing model names. The new error paragraph mentions 19 models but identifies no additional comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds supplementary sampling conditions at temperatures 0.2, 0.7, and 1.2 with top_p=0.9. Section 7 adds event- and character-level error-overlap measurements using Jaccard similarity. The original deterministic evaluation, validation set, and scoring threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two distinct investigations absent from v1: decoding-temperature sensitivity across models and prompts, and shared failures across events and characters. These substantially extend robustness and error analysis beyond the retained validation probes and event-type, length, and position analyses.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports using a shared random seed across models and prompts for the stochastic ablation. It does not report repeated-run uncertainty for that experiment. Existing bootstrap intervals, significance tests, multiplicity corrections, and annotator-agreement reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 252 main accuracy entries and matched earlier appendix results are unchanged. v2 substantially extends the findings with the stochastic result grid, reporting average drops of 0.3, 0.8, and 2.3 points relative to deterministic decoding, plus shared-error findings such as 59.1% of events being missed by at least ten models. The error analysis's stated 19-model count conflicts with Table 2's 18 rows.

T1.justification: The formal cloze definitions, audit equations, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Added threshold explanations and cloze illustrations introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs; Jaccard overlap is used as an empirical metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, research questions, and conclusion retain the same framework, feasibility claims, prompt dependence, and leading-model findings. Revised wording and the new mission statement do not redefine the core scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new experiments as evidence of decoding robustness and concentrated, shared difficulties rather than idiosyncratic model failures. It identifies socioeconomic explanations for those failures as future work and adds a mission connecting scholarship with journalism and public history. Existing language and cultural-coverage limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses annotator backgrounds and specifies metadata-based language filtering. Appendix D.4 explains the already-stated name-frequency and top-10,000 cutoffs, while D.5 clarifies existing validation tasks. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated changes to the original settings. Code and derived-data release remain prospective and conditional.

R1.justification: v2 adds Evans and Duede (2025), Spangher et al. (2024), and Sui et al. (2025, KRISTEVA), connecting the paper to knowledge production, journalistic writing, and humanities research standards. The established critical-fabulation and NLP positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section structure remain intact. v2 adds localized explanations, analysis paragraphs, appendix subsections, a Humanistic Mission Statement, and acknowledgments. It removes the preprint header and the sentence asserting IRB approval; that deletion does not establish a change in approval status.

P2.justification: v2 adds the stochastic-results table and a cloze-setup illustration, revises Figures 1–3 for presentation and label readability, and expands Table 2's caption. The original workflow figure becomes Figure 5, while retained tables are renumbered and repositioned within the same general layout.

improvement.justification: The added temperature and shared-error analyses address previously unexamined reliability questions, while threshold explanations, annotator backgrounds, and clearer figures improve transparency. The net gain is limited by missing repeated-run uncertainty and incomplete reporting of the new analyses, including an unlabeled hint condition in Table 3 and the inconsistent 19-model count.
